paragraphs.text: The Theorist takes notice of innovative battlemages.
He speaks what the futurescribes have written.
Greatness is earned, not bought.
It roams the halls for truant students, who suddenly find themselves back in class.
"Right as rain!" the saccharine double taunted.
"Bring me the underperformers. I will make them flourish." —Kwia Vigorbloom
When medical supplies are limited, her own cuttings will suffice.
It hands direction to straying minds.
In the end, the light shone, the land flourished, and the dead and vile were washed away.
"We swore to keep watch," Ajani growled through gritted teeth, "and that includes against our own."
The Theorist used his own memories to trap the parts of Jace that objected to his plans, and to ensnare the friends who wished to stop him.
Fatehold battlemages believe the best way to win a duel is to first study the outcome.
Upon death, an oracle of Arcavios returns to the very source of their world. Jace followed Jadzi's mind to witness two planes becoming one.
Quandrix believed in finding the equations of the natural world. Hexhaven disrupted the pattern of existence.
A face half remembered, a form fit to serve.
"For every living person there are generations of souls reaching out to be remembered." —Liliana the Faultless
Winged with the shards of shattered star arches, it circles above the Eradia. A rare glimmer of hope for students caught in the perilous wasteland that surrounds Jace's tower.
Vigorbloom battlemages love dueling. Opportunities to hurt sow opportunities to heal.
Battlefield medicine is as much about timing as it is healing. A perfect remedy is worthless if it comes too late.
"The future looms large over the present, and you're blocking my view."
"There is no curve. Either you succeeded, or you did not. Either way, this will be informative." —Uldaros Theorix
"I predicted your quips yesterday, Stingerquill. They weren't clever then either."
"Keep them distracted," instructed the Theorist. Chandra's doppelganger smiled, and a chill went through the air.
Theorem dreams soon became nightmares.
"No need to sneak around. Beleren knows we're here." —Garruk, to Vraska
In the Meditation Realm, Jace had seen himself reflected in a Multiverse complete in every detail. Now he only had to make it real.
Silverquill believed the word was the mightiest weapon. Hexhaven got the last one.
"Am I a person?" she asked. Jace smiled. "Yes. Your name is Tamira. But who you are is up to you."
Twisting in the wind like a strange banner, it keeps watch over the horizon and tower alike.
"The Multiverse is a work in progress. There will need to be revisions." —The Theorist, Jace Beleren
"Please, do take it personally." —Ingris Stingerquill
Every part of Jace's mind that objected to his plan had been cut away. The Theorist was all that remained.
Theorix has the most instances, by far, of posthumously awarded extra credit.
Some eclipses never exit totality.
"On the bright side, the corpus inversion spell performed as expected." —Zim, Theorix mage
Jace believed that if he could successfully merge the two Multiverses, he would remove the suffering of so many.
"Poor cadet didn't even make it to the chorus." —Miskatel, Stingerquill voxmancer
Existence can be categorically denied. You just need the right variables.
"Suffering ends at my will."
The Eradia surrounding Hexhaven is rife with mage hunters drawn to the powerful magic emanating from the school's tower.
The scrabbling of claws across stone was a symphony to Liliana's ears as she ordered the swarm against her sickeningly nice twin.
"I am the curse."
She weaves brutal insults into hypnotizing melodies, enthralling her victims to stay and listen.
The Vraska who had never known pain could not comprehend the unyielding will of the Vraska who had known too much.
The Theorist has no interest in failures.
Prismari believed art was in the eye of the beholder. Hexhaven was a harsh critic.
"Mortality is just one more parameter to define and defy."
The memory trap tormented Ajani. "Time's up, brother," said Jazal's voice inside his head. "Your vengeance, or your friends. What will it be?"
"It's important to emphasize core principles, but to win duels you must extrapolate your designs to work in a variety of formats." —*Advanced Tethering*
Nothing burns like betrayal.
"I learned this little trick from Koth." —Chandra
When Chandra needed to summon a chaotic distraction, only one form came to mind.
Stingerquill admits only the fiercest hearts.
Some puppetbeasts are monstrous machines. Others, works of art. The best are both.
He had gambled and accepted the pact, ignorant of what he stood to lose.
"What is that?! A firebreathing sphinx?" —Derenk, Hexhaven cadet
She puts the harm in harmony.
Witherbloom believed in life and death's intricate balance. Hexhaven was drawn to their unpredictable power.
"I only wish you could see the necessity of this. Your counterparts all have." —The Theorist, Jace Beleren
A solo so violent even the echoes can deafen the unprepared.
"Come on cadet, I'll show you the ropes!"
The question isn't *if* he'll make his students cry. Only when.
Konstrari frontline mages are adept at turning implements of craft into instruments of war.
Konstrari cadets are Hexhaven's front line against any threat, be it Eradian abominations or extradimensional academies.
Two Multiverses. Only one future.
"I can see the weakness in your soul. Let me cut it out of you!"
Its tongues can taste loyalty—or deceit.
"Petition the dean for additional seeds. Gaz and Dak got into the medical supplies. Again." —Divik, Vigorbloom cadet
"If we're going to fix things, we should start here. Why does no one question the Theorist?"
Lorehold believed in learning from history. Hexhaven made sure that history was brief.
Starting sprouts —Vigorbloom term for their first graft
Vigorbloom's unique graft technique requires the tender nurturing of seedlings to root seamlessly into the body and facilitate healing.
"Behold ideal symbiosis." —Kwia Vigorbloom
One wielder a fierce steward of the wilds, the other a cruel bringer of death.
Her choice made, Tam called upon the one being who could fix what Jace had done.
Garruk looked at the young, scared boy from Vryn. "I have also begun anew," he rumbled.
It was solemn work, repurposing flesh as fertile soil.
"Jace cut out all the best pieces of himself. If we find them, perhaps they can help save him."
Her specialized arrows turn targets to compost before they even hit the ground.
What doesn't adapt, dies. And what dies feeds the tarmogoyf.
Konstrari students harness leyline energy to animate their constructs. The more determined the tethermage, the more effective the puppetbeast.
It specializes in natural disorder.
Some battlevine cultivars can grasp flesh as easily as they can climb walls.
"Corridors 17-24 are now open for extra credit training. Come prepared." —Campus announcement
He had failed his final exam, but his professor had kindly offered a way to make up the work.
"Proper medical assistance is hard to find. I suggest you grow your own." —Karalgin, professor of phytomancy
Deep in their hearts, the team believed what was left of Jace could still be reasoned with.
"More fire? Is that your solution to everything?" one Chandra asked. "Works pretty well, doesn't it?" the other replied.
As realities merged, the futures she could read dwindled.
"A spark is power and freedom. Use it better than I did," Jace's voice echoed to Tam.
It's a contradiction in burns.
"I've seen hay fever hit harder than that!"
Denied all tools of necromancy, Liliana endured her least favorite feeling: boredom.
"Confidence is relative. Bolster yours by breaking theirs." —Ingris Stingerquill
Tam had offered to help and Vraska believed her.
"Today, you will be learning material repurposing and adaptation. This will be on the test."
"She will rage and burn until her fuel is expended. It's almost sad to see me like this."
"Josu's ashes choke you even now. You failed, while I will have our brother live forever," said one Liliana to the other.
As much as Liliana never wanted to see her opaline double again, she had always been loath to prematurely discard a useful tool.
Whetted against grief. Wielded with vengeance.
An eyeless guard of stone watches a forgotten annex of memory, granite feathers rustling in breezes no one thinks to remember.
It ensures students leave the Folioplex with the correct notes, theories, and ponderings.
The tower transformed to fulfill its true purpose: as a catalyst to merge the old Multiverse with the new.
All cadets wore the Eye. None discussed how it followed their every move.
Late at night it searches for students congregating where they shouldn't be.
"Too many lives have been cut short, too many of their futures untold. I can rewrite them. I can give them a voice." —The Theorist, Jace Beleren
An apothecary on wings.
Its pages surrender no words until the book has first read its prospective reader.
"Our mobile greenhouse will never be deprived of energy again. It will always align itself to the sun's path." —Vigorbloom and Konstrari joint project
Jace remembered the island. The useless original, the inner refuge. He remembered how twice he found the strength to rebuild himself from nothing.
Battlemages of Fatehold, the school of future history, sift through infinite potentials to write the future they desire.
"The wood of the theater is shaped to capture reverberations, and the resulting sound is deafening!" —Konstrari and Stingerquill joint project
The tunnels below Hexhaven murmur with ripples of first breaths.
Jace remembered the mage-rings. The first time he touched another's mind. He remembered how powerful his own could be if he were willing to find his limits.
Those who survive are stronger for it.
"Proud to announce we've invented a *voice-activated* void portal! No gestures needed!" —Stingerquill and Theorix joint project
Battlemages of Konstrari, the school of constructive arts, pour their hearts into their craft in defense of Hexhaven.
"We present a new way to calculate predictions based upon the *absence* of data." —Fatehold and Theorix joint project
Jace remembered the shadows. The inscrutable puzzle, the prisoner in the moon. He remembered how victory could be achieved by choosing not to play.
Jace remembered the gate. The dying world, the wanderers who stayed to fight. He remembered how even the most impossible problems had practical solutions.
Jace left slices of his personality trapped in his strongest memories.
Any shelter from the Theorist's gaze was a welcome one.
Jace remembered the ship. The captain who saw him through. He remembered how losing a part of himself had only made him stronger.
Battlemages of Stingerquill, the school of painful words, sharpen their tongues to cut down the unworthy.
Battlemages of Theorix, the school of esoteric mathematics, reshape reality itself to their whim.
"We've developed seeds that see their own future and self-select for the good of the species." —Vigorbloom and Fatehold joint project
Battlemages of Vigorbloom, the school of invasive healing, tend to the health of Hexhaven, no matter the cost.
"Benalia stands for hope and light. I pledge my blade to any that fall under its banner."
Inscribed are the words "I will keep watch."
"Malach, tell your mother the steelfruit harvest is abundant this cycle!"
"All mistakes can be fixed. Even you."
She is the radiant sun that shatters darkness.
"The Helpful Hero! The Daring Darling of the Tenth District!" —*Ravnica Gazette* headline
"A creative mind is a dangerous thing."
"In Sigarda's name, I will ensure your peaceful rest."
"Many wield the law as a cudgel. I prefer to use it as a shield."
The Emperor spared no comfort for the friend who had so diligently awaited her return.
"Emperor Tamiyo rules with truth, respect, and passion. She has more than earned my loyalty."
"If you have a tale worthy of telling, I would hear it, friend."
Fblthp had *definitely* made a wrong turn.
"Be at peace, child. The horrors will not claim you this night."
"Kefnet always told me to apply my knowledge. I merely chose to apply it in usurping him."
Knowledge is radiance.
When the crime is violent, call the Boros. When it's legalistic, call the Azorius. When it's complex, call him.
The Simic Combine's two brightest minds.
Everything in her wake stills, then stops.
"You can't always be perfect. Sometimes your escape has to be just good enough."
"Tolaria has stood for a thousand years. You're looking at why." —Lyra, Tolarian headmaster

"Why sure I remember Yar-Kul! Man had the most refined palate in all Otaria. I still have some of his cookbooks. Shame he went and trespassed in Krosan forest . . . There ain't a single soul who comes outta those woods unchanged." —Mister Foundforks, culinarian
"To know the Cabal is to know despair. None can stand against its legions."
The party never ends, but the guests will never arrive.
"The man who was Kytheon Iora, hero of the people, was lost long ago. I serve no one now."
"My mistakes are *mine* to fix."
Loot's value is absolute in any Multiverse, so Jace kept him locked away and hidden.
With her village destroyed, Mabel turned to the Calamity Beasts to bring down King Glarb.
Ravnica's most feared—and most adored—serial killer.
If the crime is violent, it's the Rakdos. If it's covert, it's the Dimir. If it's intricate, it's him.
"I once witnessed the power of a diamondstorm. I had to make that power my own."
No score is too small, no coin purse too big.
He had no one left to betray but himself.

"I look forward to the day when my biggest concern is the ravenous, spectral, overgrown, croaking, hulking, foulmouthed abomination that turns up every now and again just to vex us." —Field notes of Aryel, knight of Windgrace
There is no man with more bravado in all Bretagard, yet he has never exaggerated a single detail.
All of Theros is her dance floor.
His best friend was gone. Someone had to pay.
"If you can't stand the heat, get out of my way."
"My home was lost a long time ago. But maybe we can forge something new."
"I had to make a choice: save my people from Benalia, or save the land from my people. In the end, it was no choice at all."
"We've kept one foot in the past for too long. Now we walk into a better future!"
Samut doesn't pretend to know the best path, but she does know that Amonkhet will only thrive if its people keep moving forward.
"Every exit is covered. You can't run."
"Laws are made to be broken. This includes physics and thermodynamics."
"Everyone stick together. Follow my lead!"
Innistrad's moonlit nights belong to his pack and his pack alone.
Fblthp had always loved to travel.
The apex of nature's ferocity.
"I traveled with Mowu as a Planeswalker. Now I do so through Omenpaths. Neither of us are complaining about the longer walk."
"Within Loot's mind were the blueprints I needed to complete this new Multiverse. He gave me hope. Tell him that, Vraska." —Jace

"Perhaps one day I will learn how to break the hold the Consulate has over Chandra and Kiran."
"Can't cast spells with a broken mouth!"
Titanbones found he received the greatest gifts in the littlest things.
His cunning leadership of Towashi's dogs earned him the nickname "The Stray Emperor."
"Our family was born in blood, and through blood it will endure."
"Your people stand strong, Rhonas. Rest easy, you have prepared us well."
Karn forged the empty world of Mirrodin and filled it with peaceful creations.
"The sea ends where I say it does."
Mabel had learned that mother, adventurer, and protector were not all that far apart.
"Life isn't worth living without freedom of expression."
"Paths to peace are carved in flesh and stone. This is how we reform what has failed before."
"No one can remake me. Not Bolas, not Phyrexia, and not you, Jace."
"I owe the Multiverse a debt I fear I can never repay. That remedy begins now, with a first step away from the past and toward the future I wish to see."
Its orders, ancient. Its advance, ponderous. Its threat, undeniable.
A hard-earned confidence reinforced his shield. He would not falter.
"Every day, another threat. And every day, I will meet it."
"Each night, a restless terror. And each night, I will soothe it."
"I have slowed the suns themselves. Do you truly think your pulse will fare any better?"
His heart had become as hard and sharp as the diamonds he wielded.
"There is no exit. No end. Not for me."
"Llanowar is both a forest and a people. Forests are replaceable. People are not."
"Sometimes the answer is to keep moving—the sunrise at your back, the perilous expanse before you."
"I'm not looking for a way out of Duskmourn unless I can bring every other survivor along with me."
"Our prosperity comes from a forest that has always provided. We belong to Llanowar as much as it belongs to us."
A world without blemishes, a soul without anguish.
"Your scars are fault lines. I will shatter them, and you."
"I'm proud of my scars. They're who I am."
A life without rest, a soul heavy with regret.
A font of knowledge for those able to read more than a page of hexed words.
